features.description: Hard wall-clock bound on smt.Solve: exec.CommandContext with deadline max(config.Timeout, effective -T: secs) + 2s grace; own process group (Setpgid) with cmd.Cancel killing the GROUP (-pid SIGKILL, nil on ESRCH); cmd.WaitDelay so a grandchild holding the inherited pipe cannot wedge Wait; explicit context.DeadlineExceeded branch placed BEFORE the unsat/sat/unknown prefix checks, returning the existing StatusUnknown + Error 'solver timeout'. New build-tagged process_unix.go / process_windows.go LOCAL to internal/smt (NOT an import of eval_harness - that would invert the harness/core layering). Regression test uses a fake solver that ignores -T: and sleeps 30s, injected via the already-honoured SolverConfig.Z3Path.
acceptance_criteria: TestSolve_HardTimeout_FakeSolverIgnoringT returns in <10s against a fake that sleeps 30s, with Status == StatusUnknown and Error == "solver timeout" (exact string)

The fake's background grandchild pid is confirmed dead within 2s of Solve returning, via a BOUNDED syscall.Kill(pid,0) -> ESRCH poll (<=2s, 50ms interval) - no unbounded loop; Standing rule 6 applies to our own tests

NON-VACUITY PROOF: the red-first transcript (--- FAIL, elapsed ~30s, taken BEFORE solver.go is touched) is recorded verbatim in the commit body and in this JSON's notes. Do NOT use git stash / git checkout to produce it (CLAUDE.md Principle 0)
grep -c "t.Skip" internal/smt/solver_timeout_test.go == 0; the test needs no z3 and passes with AILANG_Z3_PATH=/nonexistent

No cooperative-path regression: with real z3, a 100-pigeon/99-hole instance at --timeout 1s still returns StatusUnknown/'solver timeout' in ~1.1s (Z3's own -T: fires, not ours). If z3 is absent, say so OUT LOUD rather than silently skipping this check
go test ./internal/smt/... green; existing TestSolve_*_Z3 and TestSolve_Z3NotFound unchanged and passing
cmd/ailang/verify.go and cmd/ailang/ai_check.go NOT modified - git diff --stat shows only internal/smt/

scope_decisions.z3version_in_scope: IN SCOPE (M2). Same defect class, same file, same binary, and it is on the header path of every human-mode verify. It is the only other exec.Command in internal/smt (verified: grep returns exactly two sites). Cost ~20 LOC once M1's helper exists. Leaving it would mean the audit found a second instance and knowingly shipped it - the exact anti-pattern CLAUDE.md Principle 3 names.
scope_decisions.total_run_budget: OUT OF SCOPE - M3 files a follow-up issue. A real residual (N calls = N bounds, not one run bound), but --timeout is DOCUMENTED as per-function in two commands; a total budget changes documented CLI semantics and needs decisions this sprint has no mandate for (new flag vs overload the existing one? partial-results JSON shape when the budget expires mid-run? does ai-check's consumer contract change?). Doing it quietly here would be the silent expansion the brief warns against.
scope_decisions.shared_procgroup_package: OUT - note only. Extracting internal/procgroup and refactoring eval_harness onto it is correct DRY but edits the guard currently protecting banked eval runs, for zero functional gain. Principle 3 asks us not to miss other instances of the BUG (M2 covers that); it is not a mandate to refactor a working guard in another layer.
scope_decisions.subsecond_timeout_truncation: OUT - noted in the plan. int(config.Timeout.Seconds()) floors --timeout 900ms to -T:5. Pre-existing and orthogonal; the max(...) bound means it causes no regression here.
